summary:
### TL;DR
- Six GitHub Copilot models will be deprecated across all Copilot experiences on **December 14, 2026**. Update any workflows or integrations that pin them. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-upcoming-deprecation-of-selected-github-copilot-models-in-december))
- You can now turn code scanning's AI Scan for repositories on or off through the REST API at the organization and repository levels. This is in public preview and uses a new `repository_scan` property. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-manage-ai-scan-for-repositories-using-the-rest-api))
- Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now generally available in Copilot. It is the suggested replacement for Gemini 3.8 Flash. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-gemini-4-hydrogen-in-github-copilot))

### Action required
- **Copilot model deprecations, effective 2026-12-14.** The models below go away in Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions. Move workflows and integrations to the alternatives before that date. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-upcoming-deprecation-of-selected-github-copilot-models-in-december))

  | Deprecated model | Suggested alternative |
  |---|---|
  | Claude Fable 5 | Claude Fable 5.2 |
  | Claude Haiku 4.5 | Claude Haiku 5.5 |
  | Gemini 3.8 Flash | Gemini 4 Hydrogen |
  | Gemini 4 Argon | Gemini 4 Carbon |
  | Grok 4.6 | Grok 4.7 |
  | Kimi K3 | To be announced |

  - **Haiku 4.5 exception:** individual Copilot subscribers on annual plans keep access to Claude Haiku 4.5.
  - **Business and Enterprise:** under default model enablement, the alternatives turn on automatically. If an admin has turned off the global default or disabled a model, enable the alternatives through their model policies in Copilot settings.
  - **Cleanup:** you don't need to remove the deprecated models yourself.

### Security improvements
- **REST API control for AI Scan for repositories (public preview).** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-manage-ai-scan-for-repositories-using-the-rest-api))
  - **Endpoints:** set `repository_scan` to `enabled` or `disabled` on `GET`/`PATCH /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/ai-scan` and `GET`/`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/ai-scan`. This lets you roll out the setting with scripts or infrastructure as code.
  - **Inheritance:** it works the same way as the existing `pr_scan` setting.
    - If the organization disables it, its repositories can't enable it.
    - If the organization enables it, repositories inherit it and can opt out individually.
    - If the enterprise policy doesn't allow AI Scan, the request returns a 422 error.
  - **Atomic updates:** you can set `pr_scan` and `repository_scan` in one request. If either change is blocked, you get a 422 and neither setting changes.
  - **Enabling doesn't start a scan.** Users with write access run scans on demand, and each scan consumes GitHub Code Security AI credits.
  - **Who can manage it:** organization owners and security managers control the organization setting. Repository admins can opt out individual repositories.
  - **Availability:** public repositories owned by organizations, and private or internal repositories with GitHub Code Security or GitHub Advanced Security. An enterprise owner must allow AI Scan in the enterprise policy first. GitHub Enterprise Server isn't supported.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **[AI Scan for repositories](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-scan-for-repositories):** a new section, "Managing AI Scan for repositories with the REST API," explains how to use `repository_scan`. It confirms the API follows the same organization and repository rules as the settings page. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/37824760acddef72c617e62000a10f0188b8e6dc))
- **[AI-powered security detections](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-powered-security-detections):** now names `pr_scan` (AI Scan for pull requests) and `repository_scan` (AI Scan for repositories) as the properties on the same AI Scan endpoints. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/37824760acddef72c617e62000a10f0188b8e6dc))
- **[AI Scan overview](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-scan):** adds a note that both features can be managed through the REST API at organization and repository levels. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/37824760acddef72c617e62000a10f0188b8e6dc))
- **[Configure global settings](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-global-settings):** the organization setup steps for AI Scan for repositories now point to the REST API option. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/37824760acddef72c617e62000a10f0188b8e6dc))

changelog.title: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in December
changelog.text: We will deprecate the following models across all GitHub Copilot experiences (including Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions) on December 14, 2026: Model Deprecation date Suggested alternative Claude Fable 5 2026-12-14 Claude Fable 5.2 Claude Haiku 4.5* 2026-12-14 Claude Haiku 5.5 Gemini 3.8 Flash 2026-12-14 Gemini 4 Hydrogen Gemini 4 Argon 2026-12-14 Gemini 4 Carbon Grok 4.6 2026-12-14 Grok 4.7 Kimi K3 2026-12-14 To be announced *Claude Haiku 4.5 will remain available to individual GitHub Copilot subscribers on annual plans. The deprecation of Claude Haiku 4.5 does not apply to these customers. Please update your workflows and integrations to use the supported models before this date. Under default model enablement, the suggested alternatives are automatically enabled for Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business customers unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disabled the model. If you’ve turned off the global default, you can enable access to the alternative models through their model policies in Copilot settings. Once enabled, users will see the model in the Copilot Chat model selector in supported GitHub Copilot experiences. No action is required to remove the models after they have been deprecated. GitHub Enterprise customers with questions or concerns are encouraged to contact their account team for assistance. Share your feedback To learn more about the models available in Copilot, see our documentation on supported models . Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in December appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot
changelog.text: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Google’s latest Flash model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for fast, efficient agentic coding, tool use, and multistep workflows, with improved instruction following over Gemini 3.8 Flash. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Copilot SDK Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Hydrogen through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API
changelog.text: You can now turn GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for repositories on or off with the REST API at the organization and repository levels. This public preview adds a repository_scan setting to the existing AI Scan enablement endpoints. You can roll out AI Scan for repositories with scripts and infrastructure as code instead of changing settings one organization or repository at a time. Manage AI Scan for repositories at scale Set the repository_scan property to enabled or disabled on the AI Scan enablement endpoints : GET and PATCH /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/ai-scan GET and PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/ai-scan The setting works the same way as the existing pr_scan setting for AI Scan for pull requests: When an organization disables AI Scan for repositories, its repositories can’t enable it When an organization enables it, its repositories inherit the setting and can opt out individually When an enterprise policy doesn’t allow AI Scan, requests to enable it return a 422 error You can update pr_scan and repository_scan in the same request. If either change is blocked, the request returns a 422 error and neither setting changes. Turning on AI Scan for repositories doesn’t start a scan. Users with write access still run scans on demand, and each scan consumes GitHub Code Security AI credits. Who can use it Organization owners and security managers can manage the organization setting. Repository administrators can opt individual repositories out. AI Scan for repositories is available for public repositories owned by organizations and for private or internal repositories with GitHub Code Security or GitHub Advanced Security. Enterprise owners must first allow AI Scan in the enterprise policy. GitHub Enterprise Server isn’t supported. To get started, see REST API endpoints for code scanning and AI Scan for a repository’s backlog . Join the discussion in the GitHub Community . The post Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
